b) B offers a tiny chance of a huge upside ($10,000) versus a modest certain $1,000; this is the canonical temptation for an extreme risk-seeker who focuses “almost solely on the best possible outcome.”  
c) Would they select A? **No.** A level −3 agent would nearly always prefer the 1% chance at $10,000 despite the much lower EV and disastrous downside. So they would not reliably choose A.

**Lower bound = −2**

c) Would they select A? **Yes.** Extreme risk aversion perfectly matches choosing the guaranteed insurance.
